newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: More strikes planned in Western Australia.
newsitem.headline: More strikes planned in Western Australia.

text.p: Members of the 18,000-strong Australian Manufacturing Workers' Union in Western Australia will go on strike for 24 hours from midnight Monday in protest against proposed changes to industrial relations laws.

AMWU assistant secretary Jock Ferguson said the strike would hit the printing industry, major manufacturers, heavy engineering construction, mining maintenance and various other miscellaneous manufacturing outlets.
"The majority of those 18,000 members will go out between midnight tonight and midnight tomorrow," Ferguson said.
"In those areas where we aren't the principal union our members will go out on Thursday when the CEPU (Communications Electrical and Plumbing Union) is going out for 24 hours."

The campaign against the Labour Relations Legislation Amendment Bill has involved a series of stoppages over the past two weeks. The initial target was the state's major power utility, Western Power. More recently it was fuel supplies.

On Monday, fuel tanker drivers returned to work after a four-day strike which caused many service stations in Perth to run out and prompted the union members to provide emergency supplies on a voluntary basis over the weekend.

The state's peak union organisation, The Trades and Labour Council, which is co-ordinating the campaign, has threatened international sanctions through the Australian Council of Trade Unions and the International Labor Organisation.
The bill includes provisions for compulsory pre-strike secret ballots, which the unions say are unnecessarily complicated and time-consuming, and majority membership support for political donations.
It is currently being debated in the state's legislative council where the government holds a one-seat majority.
